question: C56 found 90 residue rows whose match sits in an excluded branch. Which of those exclusions does the PRODUCER itself consider blocking?

the_producer_distinguishes_two_severitie.mark_lossy: telemetry is incomplete; the action window is still exact
the_producer_distinguishes_two_severitie.mark_attribution_unsafe: calls mark_lossy AND records an attribution_unsafe reason -- the action attribution is not observable from the engine delta
the_producer_distinguishes_two_severitie.exposed_as: the branch JSON carries lossy (list), attribution_unsafe (bool) and attribution_unsafe_reasons (list) as separate fields

the_consumer_collapses_them: engine_transition_differential.py:1396 reads only branch['lossy'], which mark_attribution_unsafe also writes to. So a branch the renderer flagged as merely telemetry-incomplete is skipped exactly as if its attribution were unobservable. The severity the producer took care to express is discarded at the boundary.
the_63_should_stay_excluded: For those the renderer is right: the attribution genuinely is not observable, and admitting them could manufacture a false MATCH, which hides a real difference. C56 warned against exactly this and the warning survives -- it applies to 63 of the 90, not to all of them.
the_27_are_the_finding: Their only marker is attract_immobilization_source_unknown, whose own source comment says: 'That omission is telemetry-only because the public action window itself is exact.' The renderer emits a full |cant|...|Attract line for these branches. It states they are exact for comparison and the consumer discards them anyway.
the_fix: make the skip decision read attribution_unsafe rather than lossy. It is a matcher change, so no rebuild and no fingerprint movement, and it is justified by the producer's own published contract rather than by a judgement about what is safe to admit.
ceiling: 27 is a CANDIDATE population. The test is net HP on both slots while the matcher compares component decompositions, so some of the 27 may still diverge. Not a predicted delta.
a_measurement_error_worth_recording: My first pass reported 122 errors and 20 lossy-only, because I read attribution_unsafe as a list when it is a bool -- list(True) raises. The 122 'errors' were the attribution-unsafe branches, i.e. the majority answer, silently discarded into an error bucket. Had I not checked what the field actually contained I would have reported 20 as the finding and missed that 63 of the 90 must stay excluded.
does_not_reach_a_pass: no code changed; unattributed stays at 366

measured.ceiling_was: 27 candidates; 27 cleared, so the ceiling was exact this time

invariants.no family may grow: ONE EXCEPTION, recorded rather than glossed: LS_capped_lethal_shape goes 463 -> 464. A single row re-attributed between two documented families, not laundering at scale -- but it is a literal violation of the invariant I registered in C55, so it is stated here instead of being absorbed into the headline.

no_fingerprint_change: this is a matcher edit, so the engine fingerprint stays at c50da60a and the era-stamped adjudications survive; the differential hash changes, so the family audit was re-derived (reports/c57_family_bucket_audit.json, no family OPEN)
